title: At Disconnect the source turns local before the phone's record is drawn, so a render in between can count the cloud's epoch under the phone's name
evidence: Done: ShownRecord.open(source:shown:drawn:phoneDrawn:) replaces open(shown:drawn:): local, it is the store on the phone's record (store.source.erase == nil); connected, as S72. RootView's countable reads it, Cover.countable is deleted, so the Disconnect window counts nothing and the phone's land flips the key and takes the count, even at an equal epoch. Reminders: the extra bump at the land only moves the token and drops the fallback epoch; nothing removes a notification, so an equal record keeps its reminders until the next refresh (ReminderSchedulerTests S73 pin). From the S72 work. ios/HealthRoadmap/Sync/CloudSync.swift:253-254 queues store.showPhone() then sends .disconnectEnded, so sync.provider is nil and RootView's source (App/RootView.swift:189) is "" while showPhone still waits on the engine's loadPhone (MyData/RecordStore.swift showPhone). The store is still .cloud, then .leaving, and still draws the cloud's record. The source change fires onChange(of: shownRecord) (RootView.swift:121), recordChanged runs, and Cover.countable("", …) (App/FirstRun.swift Cover.countable) is true, so takeCount (RootView.swift:217-220) can store the cloud record's eraseEpoch under "". After the copy-down the epochs are almost always equal, so no false erase was found. Design note first; touches the store's source. Suggested fix: the local case also requires the store on .phone (store.source.erase == nil). Test: Disconnect, a render between .disconnectEnded and the phone's draw, no count taken until the phone's record lands.
